## 足球 · 30 items

The football world is consumed by World Cup countdown stories: player health updates, team preparations, and a high-profile officiating controversy dominate the past 24 hours. Key narratives revolve around Christian Eriksen's recovery, Brazil's Neymar progress, and the Netherlands' injury blow, while off-pitch stories like the Somali referee denial and Platini's legal action add layers of intrigue.

- **Eriksen's recovery** remains the most uplifting story; he has been discharged from hospital and is 'doing well' ([ESPN](https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/49001056/christian-eriksen-collapse-heart-condition-denmark-recovery), [Sky Sports](https://www.skysports.com/football/news/12040/13551798/christian-eriksen-doing-well-and-at-home-after-collapsing-during-denmark-friendly)). His collapse during Denmark's friendly against Ukraine raised immediate concerns, but rapid medical care ensured a positive outcome.
- **Neymar's calf injury** is improving faster than expected; an MRI confirmed 'good progress' ([ESPN](https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/49002184/brazil-mri-neymar-good-progress-injury)), boosting Brazil's World Cup hopes. - **Argentina** will field Lionel Messi in their final friendly against Iceland, but manager Lionel Scaloni will manage his minutes to avoid risks ([ESPN](https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/49004047/argentina-avoid-risks-messi-play-friendly)).

- **Somali referee Omar Artan** was denied entry to the US and removed from the World Cup officials list, a blow to diversity in officiating ([ESPN](https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/49002985/somali-referee-world-cup-denied-entry-united-states), [BBC](https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cnv9drg0qzgo)).

With World Cup kickoff just days away, the focus will shift from friendly matches to final squad decisions and last-minute fitness tests. The Eriksen incident remains a reminder of the risks athletes face, but his recovery offers hope.
